entry.title: Navi Pillay, former UN human rights chief, wins Nobel Peace Prize
entry.summary: Pillay is recognised for her "efforts to promote peace and international law", the Norwegian Nobel Committee says.

entry.title: Firing squad execution to be livestreamed, Pentagon says
entry.summary: Pete Hegseth says the execution will be public, but a legal expert says the "unprecedented" decision is on "uncertain legal terrain".

entry.title: Fort Hood survivor supports gunman's execution by firing squad but questions livestream
entry.summary: Alonzo Lunsford tells the BBC the punishment befits the crime but he has some doubts whether the public should be able to watch it.

entry.title: France promises 3,000 extra teachers in first step to calm student protests
entry.summary: Education minister Edouard Geffray makes the offer after another day of sometimes violent demonstrations by high-school students.

entry.title: Ethiopia warns Eritrea it will defend itself after troops cross border
entry.summary: Truckloads of Eritrean soldiers have been seen driving into Ethiopia, which has reportedly responded with drone strikes.

entry.title: Suspect linked to Monaco bomb attack on millionaire speaks to BBC
entry.summary: Vitalii Zhykovych gives his own account of the attempted assassination of Ukrainian-born businessman Vadym Yermolayev.

entry.title: Thieves steal 30,000 bottles of wine worth €5m in Italy, reports say
entry.summary: The heist at the Florence-based winery is believed to be one of the largest thefts of its kind in Italy.

entry.title: ICE agent shoots man in New York City
entry.summary: The mayor of New York expressed outrage at the shooting which the Department of Homeland Security said happened during the arrest of a "criminal illegal alien".

entry.title: Crazy Rich Asians to return as TV show with original film's stars
entry.summary: It will pick up after the hit 2018 film, starring Constance Wu, Henry Golding, Michelle Yeoh and Ronny Chieng.

entry.title: Doctor accused of 1994 Rwanda genocide offences to face trial in UK
entry.summary: Dr Vincent Brown was allegedly a "leader" or "supervisor" of violent acts carried out by others in the early days of the genocide.

entry.title: Three Saudi nationals killed in Houthi attacks on Riyadh airport
entry.summary: The missile attacks come amid an escalation in fighting between the Iran-backed group and Saudi Arabia, which backs Yemen's government.

entry.title: Two Renoir paintings stolen from French museum are recovered
entry.summary: The two works were seized last month when thieves cut through a fence and smashed a window at the Renoir Museum on the French Riviera.

entry.title: Cars torched and shops looted as anti-migrant violence erupts in South Africa
entry.summary: South Africa has experienced recurrent outbreaks of violence, often targeting migrants from neighbouring countries.

entry.title: Christa Pike has 'profound' health turnaround after botched execution, lawyers say
entry.summary: Pike's lawyers say her recovery is "remarkable" as they give an update on her condition after she survived an execution attempt by lethal injection.

entry.title: Fired OpenAI researchers say they were let go for 'prioritising safety'
entry.summary: The AI firm instead claims the researchers were fired for mishandling sensitive information.

entry.title: Adidas sues Australian label White Fox over four stripes design
entry.summary: The German sportswear brand wants the Sydney-based label to stop selling the clothes and pay damages.

entry.title: 'Bold and inventive' Canadian poet Anne Carson wins Nobel Literature Prize
entry.summary: Carson, 76, is celebrated for works that often cross boundaries between poetry, fiction and scholarship.

entry.title: Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture
entry.summary: The new accusations relate to the alleged torture of US citizens held in Venezuela while Maduro was in power.

entry.title: Teacher who sexually abused pupil back in Indonesia jail after BBC investigation
entry.summary: Mochamad Subchi Azal Tsani had been secretly released on parole in 2025, after serving less than half his sentence.

entry.title: Italy approves elections overhaul as opposition accuse Meloni of 'scam'
entry.summary: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni says the move will deliver more stable government, but opposition parties say her aim is to stay in power.

entry.title: US deportations to African countries unlawful and exploit suffering, rights group says
entry.summary: More than 500 migrants have been expelled from the US to African countries, HRW says, citing US data.

entry.title: Outspoken Indian actor Nana Patekar dies suddenly at 75
entry.summary: Known for his intense performances, Patekar carved out a distinctive place in Indian cinema.

entry.title: Residents airlifted to safety after flooding in central Chile
entry.summary: The Mapocho river has burst its banks after an unusually large amount of rain fell in recent days.

entry.title: Zambia signs US health deal after disputes over data-sharing
entry.summary: The US will provide $1.5bn (£1.1bn) under the deal that was negotiated after Trump cut USAID funding.

entry.title: Tanker hit by multiple projectiles in Gulf off Qatar, maritime agency says
entry.summary: Casualties have been reported on the vessel, identified by a maritime intelligence firm as the oil and chemical tanker, Acers.

entry.title: South Korea recalls Ukraine envoy over prisoner-of-war row
entry.summary: It is the latest in a diplomatic spat after Kyiv disclosed that two North Korean prisoners were transferred to Seoul.

entry.title: Arizona congressional candidate says she was raped while repairing campaign sign
entry.summary: Bernadette Greene-Placentia says her memory of the attack is spotty and that she was knocked unconscious.

entry.title: Russian strikes and approaching winter force some in Kyiv to pack bags and flee
entry.summary: A renewed Russian campaign of strikes on power and energy infrastructure has made some contemplate leaving Ukraine's capital.

entry.title: Meet India's feisty Gen Z protester who is taking on Modi
entry.summary: Neha Bora has emerged as one of the most recognisable faces from India's recent Gen Z-led protests.

entry.title: Mark Zuckerberg has an image problem - so why is Meta's business booming?
entry.summary: A new film paints the Meta founder as a villain. But the tech firm seems immune to bad publicity, writes our North America tech correspondent.

entry.title: Why Elon Musk is taking on India's richest man over Starlink
entry.summary: Musk has taken pot-shots at Reliance owner Mukesh Ambani as Starlink struggles to launch in India.

entry.title: Why is it so hard to put out Indonesian fires shrouding the region in toxic smog?
entry.summary: We explain why Indonesia’s peatland fires are so difficult to battle and produce so much haze.

entry.title: Fleeing Kyiv for the countryside ahead of winter
entry.summary: A Kyiv resident told the BBC she has moved away from "everything that can be a Russian target" as Ukraine braces for another cold winter under intense attacks.

entry.title: ​​USS Lincoln finally docks in San Diego after 10-month mission
entry.summary: The US aircraft carrier was set to return in May but the war with Iran has kept it at sea on one of the longest deployments ever.

entry.title: Watch: Why was the sign at the British consulate in East Jerusalem removed?
entry.summary: The consulate, first established in 1838, was set to be closed by the Israeli government in retaliation for UK sanctions.
